**Verdict:** Kill the false alarms first; leave the rotation alone. 1-in-6 weeks is healthy—burnout is coming from waking up for zero-value noise.

**1. Audit last 4 wks (~40 pages) this week**
- Group by alert rule; top 2–3 monitors usually drive ~80% of false alarms.
- Enforce one bar: page *only* on active user impact (or imminent SLO burn) requiring immediate human action.
- Downgrade everything else (CPU/disk thresholds, self-healing blips, wait-til-9am issues) to Slack/tickets, or delete.

**2. Give on-call unilateral kill power**
- On-call eng can immediately mute/downgrade any alert that pages them w/o requiring action. Review later, never debate at 3am.

**3. Dedicate on-call week to reliability**
- Pull on-call eng off sprint feature work; spend the week fixing root causes of recurring pages + tuning thresholds.
- Run a 15-min weekly handoff review: every off-hours page must produce a ticket to fix the system, raise the threshold, or delete the alert.

**4. Stop bleeding morale immediately**
- Mandatory comp time: paged between 11pm–7am = next morning/day off, no questions.

**Target:** <2 off-hours pages/wk. Only revisit schedule structure (e.g., splitting Mon–Thu / Fri–Sun) if *real* emergencies stay high once noise hits zero.
